## Exercise 6: one function, one hardware objective {#arithmetic-objective}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Input: arithmetic function**

```mlir
func.func @ex6_integer_mul(
    %lhs : i8 {hw.name = "lhs"},
    %rhs : i8 {hw.name = "rhs"})
    -> (i8 {hw.name = "product"}) {
  %product = arith.muli %lhs, %rhs : i8
  return %product : i8
}
```
:::

::: {.column width="4%"}
$$\Longrightarrow$$
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
**Objective: combinational module**

```mlir
hw.module @ex6_integer_mul(
    in %lhs : i8,
    in %rhs : i8,
    out product : i8) {
  %product = comb.mul %lhs, %rhs : i8
  hw.output %product : i8
}
```
:::
::::

The analogies are visible, but they are not equivalent transformations:

| MLIR source | Hardware analogue | What is missing? |
|---|---|---|
| `func.func` / `return` | `hw.module` / `hw.output` | module and interface policy |
| `arith.muli` | `comb.mul` | a supported operation mapping |

`func` and `arith` are upstream MLIR dialects. `hw` and `comb` express the
CIRCT hardware objective.

## `map-arith-to-comb` draws a deliberate line {#arithmetic-map-contract}

```{.text code-line-numbers="2,4|5-6|9-13"}
def MapArithToCombPass : Pass<"map-arith-to-comb"> {
  let summary = "Map arith ops to combinational logic";
  let description = [{
    A pass which does a simple `arith` to `comb` mapping wherever possible.
    This pass will not convert:
    * floating point operations
    * operations using `vector`-typed values

    This does not intend to be the definitive lowering/HLS pass of `arith`
    operations in CIRCT (hence the name "map" instead of e.g. "lower").
    Rather, it provides a simple way (mostly for testing purposes) to map
    `arith` operations.
  }];
}
```

[CIRCT `Transforms/Passes.td`, pinned `firtool-1.147.0` source](https://github.com/llvm/circt/blob/firtool-1.147.0/include/circt/Transforms/Passes.td#L56-L76)

The failure is the documented boundary of the pass. Our exercise supplies one
concrete floating-point lowering.

## Eight bits encode several numerical regimes {#arithmetic-e4m3-format}

::: {.bit-layout}
::: {.bit-field .sign}
**s**

`[7]`

<small>sign · 1 bit</small>
:::
::: {.bit-field .exponent}
**eeee**

`[6:3]`

<small>biased exponent · 4 bits</small>
:::
::: {.bit-field .fraction}
**mmm**

`[2:0]`

<small>stored fraction · 3 bits</small>
:::
:::

| Regime | Encoding | Value |
|---|---|---|
| zero | `e = 0000`, `m = 000` | $0$ |
| subnormal | `e = 0000`, `m != 000` | $(-1)^s 2^{-6}(m/8)$ |
| normal | `e != 0000` | $(-1)^s 2^{e-7}(1+m/8)$ |
| NaN | `e = 1111`, `m = 111` | not a number |

`f8E4M3FN` has bias 7, finite values up to 448, and no infinity.
[@micikevicius2022fp8]

## Subnormals fill the gap around zero {#arithmetic-e4m3-axis}

![](assets/images/e4m3-number-line.svg){fig-alt="Positive E4M3FN values near zero, with subnormal and normal ranges distinguished" width="100%"}

| Bits | Hex | Value |
|---|---:|---:|
| `0 0000 001` | `0x01` | $2^{-9}$ = 0.001953125 |
| `0 0000 111` | `0x07` | $7 \times 2^{-9}$ = 0.013671875 |
| `0 0001 000` | `0x08` | $2^{-6}$ = 0.015625 |

The sign bit mirrors these points onto the negative axis.

## The same format spans tiny values to 448 {#arithmetic-e4m3-values}

| Hex | Fields `s eeee mmm` | Value |
|---:|---|---:|
| `0x00` | `0 0000 000` | 0 |
| `0x08` | `0 0001 000` | $2^{-6}$ |
| `0x30` | `0 0110 000` | 0.5 |
| `0x38` | `0 0111 000` | 1 |
| `0x3C` | `0 0111 100` | 1.5 |
| `0x41` | `0 1000 001` | 2.25 |
| `0x7E` | `0 1111 110` | 448 |
| `0x7F` | `0 1111 111` | NaN |

Less precision buys a smaller representation and more operations per watt;
the exact rounding and exceptional-value rules remain part of the contract.

## Exercise 7: replace the floating-point DAG {#arithmetic-pass-goal}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="54%"}
```mlir
func.func @e4m3fn_mul(
    %lhs : i8, %rhs : i8) -> i8 {
  %lhsf = arith.bitcast %lhs
      : i8 to f8E4M3FN
  %rhsf = arith.bitcast %rhs
      : i8 to f8E4M3FN
  %productf = arith.mulf
      %lhsf, %rhsf : f8E4M3FN
  %product = arith.bitcast %productf
      : f8E4M3FN to i8
  return %product : i8
}
```
:::

::: {.column width="46%"}
![](assets/images/digital-design/yosys/e4m3_mul_parts.svg){fig-alt="Word-level DAG of the sign, exponent, and significand paths for E4M3 multiplication" width="100%"}

The custom pass replaces the complete `bitcast` → `mulf` → `bitcast` island
with an `i8` `comb` datapath.
:::
::::

The course helper `--tutorial-func-to-hw` still handles the function boundary.

## E4M3 multiplication exposes three paths {#arithmetic-multiply-paths}

| Path | Normal operands |
|---|---|
| sign | $s_r = s_a \oplus s_b$ |
| exponent | $e_r = e_a + e_b - 7$, then adjust after normalization |
| significand | $(1.m_a) \times (1.m_b)$: four bits by four bits |

::: {.fragment}
For example, `0x3C × 0x3C` is $1.5 \times 1.5 = 2.25$, encoded as `0x41`.
:::

Normalization and rounding bring the raw eight-bit significand product back
to three stored fraction bits.

## The normal path is already a circuit {#arithmetic-normal-path}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%"}
```mlir
%sa = comb.extract %lhs from 7 : (i8) -> i1
%sb = comb.extract %rhs from 7 : (i8) -> i1
%sign = comb.xor %sa, %sb : i1

%fa = comb.extract %lhs from 0 : (i8) -> i3
%fb = comb.extract %rhs from 0 : (i8) -> i3
%ma4 = comb.concat %one, %fa : i1, i3
%mb4 = comb.concat %one, %fb : i1, i3
%ma = comb.concat %zero4, %ma4 : i4, i4
%mb = comb.concat %zero4, %mb4 : i4, i4
%raw = comb.mul %ma, %mb : i8
```
:::

::: {.column width="51%"}
![](assets/images/digital-design/yosys/e4m3_mul_parts.svg){fig-alt="Word-level schematic of the sign, exponent, and significand paths for normal E4M3 operands" width="100%"}
:::
::::

## Normal arithmetic is only the first checkpoint {#arithmetic-special-cases}

| Case | Required action |
|---|---|
| zero | return signed zero |
| subnormal input | use a significand without the hidden leading one |
| subnormal result | shift into the gradual-underflow range |
| discarded bits | round to nearest, ties to even |
| overflow | return the signed E4M3FN NaN encoding |
| NaN | return an E4M3FN NaN encoding |

The supplied SystemVerilog reference implements this complete contract.

## Match the complete floating-point island {#arithmetic-pass-shape}

```cpp
class LowerE4M3FNMulPattern
    : public OpRewritePattern<arith::BitcastOp> {
  LogicalResult matchAndRewrite(
      arith::BitcastOp outputCast,
      PatternRewriter &rewriter) const override {
    auto mul = outputCast.getIn()
        .getDefiningOp<arith::MulFOp>();
    auto lhsCast = mul.getLhs()
        .getDefiningOp<arith::BitcastOp>();
    auto rhsCast = mul.getRhs()
        .getDefiningOp<arith::BitcastOp>();
    // Build the i8 comb network from lhsCast and rhsCast.
  }
};
```

The outer bitcast is the root because it and the replacement both produce
`i8`.
